nodes.label: Conversation Window (Talk/Story/Journal/Time/Travel tabs)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the wood-and-parchment design with a live resident portrait; dialogue types out with soft blips and residents speak in wordless hums instead of vanilla villager sounds.

nodes.label: Guard Pursuit Limits
nodes.rationale: Aggressors are remembered 60 seconds; combat stays within 32 blocks of the starting point; guards never load distant chunks, teleport, build bridges or clear terrain, and anger clears on unload/restart.

nodes.label: Guard Equipment Exchange (Equip held item)
nodes.rationale: Peaceful players may swap a guard's weapon/armor without friendship; recruited guards accept only their owner. One physical item is consumed even in Creative and the previous piece is returned.

nodes.label: Initial Guard Equipment (UUID-selected iron/chainmail)
nodes.rationale: Weapon plus four armor pieces, exactly two iron and two chainmail chosen by UUID; a saved marker prevents regeneration on reload, conversion, upgrade or breakage.

nodes.label: Unlimited Safe Archer Arrows
nodes.rationale: Archers have uncollectable unlimited arrows; they check the firing path and arrows cannot injure villagers, iron golems or non-target players; arrows remember the guard level when fired.

nodes.label: Automatic Village Defense (Knights and Archers)
nodes.rationale: Knights use swords; archers fire bows and retreat within four blocks. Guards scan 16 blocks twice a second; idle guards keep ordinary jobs, trades, sleep and social behavior; children and NoAI residents do not fight.

nodes.label: villager_predators Entity Tag
nodes.rationale: Data-pack replaceable target list (zombies, illagers, ravagers, zoglins...); creepers are always excluded and idle player-hostile mobs are not targets.

nodes.label: Adventure Companions (Follow/Wait/Return home)
nodes.rationale: One companion per player and one owner per resident; Overworld only, no portals, and pathfinding never builds bridges or alters terrain.

nodes.label: Never Hand-Edit Compiled Assets
nodes.rationale: Wardrobe PNG/JSON under assets/villagefriends/wardrobe and resident_animations/*.json are compiled from Python modules; edit the source module and rerun the generator with --check.

nodes.label: Future Real-Time Knockout Controller
nodes.rationale: Planned system that will consume the medical treatment contract; the existing companion rescue/recovery behavior is retained meanwhile.

nodes.label: Medical Treatment Contract
nodes.rationale: MedicalSupplyItem.treatment(): Smelling Salts restore 0.20 max health, Revival Tonic 1.00, Bandage Wrap adds 12 real-time hours. Items do not revive yet; the controller should validate the patient, apply on the server and consume only on success.

nodes.label: Downed Companion Rescue
nodes.rationale: A lethal injury leaves a recruited companion downed with identity and equipment intact; after one minute without rescue they recover at home and remember the interrupted outing.

nodes.label: Bread, Stew and Coffee Consumables
nodes.rationale: Bread heals two, stew heals six and returns a bowl, coffee grants Speed I for 30s and returns its mug; effects run on the server.

nodes.label: 24 New Items and 41 Recipes
nodes.rationale: Medical supplies, coffee mugs, bread, stew, rain gear, ten profession uniforms and five tool props; tools are registered handheld props whose behaviors are future systems.

nodes.label: Wearable Uniforms and Rain Gear
nodes.rationale: Twelve chest-slot wearables with no armor protection; can be given to companions via Travel -> Equip held item.

nodes.label: Foundation Catalog (foundation-catalog.json)
nodes.rationale: Documentation data for verification/integrations rather than a reloadable registry configuration.

nodes.label: Future Spatial Bed Scanner
nodes.rationale: Not implemented; House Plaques instantiate the Phase 1 block entity with empty scan hooks. Doors are treated as room boundaries even when open.

nodes.label: Room/Structure Catalog (structure-catalog.json)
nodes.rationale: Reproducible catalog recording room bounds, probes, bed feet, doors, fixtures and connectors as future scanner fixtures.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Foundation Gameplay Verification
nodes.rationale: FoundationGameTest runs first and validates registry/POI loading, recipes, exact potion matching, trades, placement/drops, natural acquisition of all ten professions and save/reload; focused via -PfoundationOnly.

nodes.label: Native Trade Sets (50 sets, 100 offers)
nodes.rationale: Two offers per profession level across five levels; prices are initial balance choices editable in data/villagefriends/trade_set.

nodes.label: 17 New Foundation Blocks
nodes.rationale: Eleven workstations plus Village Bench, Campfire Bench, Apothecary Cot, House Plaque, Notice Board and Command Desk; four facing states, matching collision, recipe, loot. Benches declare planned capacity two (BENCH_CAPACITY); seating is later work.

nodes.label: Registration Order (blocks, items, block entities, professions)
nodes.norm_label: registration order (blocks, items, block entities, professions)
nodes.rationale: VillageFoundation.register() runs from VillageFriends.onInitialize() before narrative content loading.

nodes.label: Codex Phase 1: Registry & Item Foundation
nodes.rationale: Register professions, POIs, blocks, items and block entity types with usable assets, and expose hooks for later controllers; uses vanilla job acquisition/trading and the existing resident entity, so no new entity type is needed.

nodes.label: Ten New Professions and Workstations
nodes.rationale: Knight, Archer, Cook, Tavern Keeper, Apothecary, Painter, Bard, Tailor, Carpenter, Scholar. Each workstation is a job POI (one ticket, range one) tagged acquirable_job_site; Sewing Tables and Archives are distinct anchors so vanilla looms, lecterns and barrels keep their original professions.

nodes.label: Layered JSON Blueprints (tools/village_blueprints)
nodes.rationale: One blueprint per template recording its design source and checksum; design_village.py never overwrites a hand-edited blueprint without --force, so hand edits are never silently lost. Geometry stays in designs/blueprints, not in the compiler.

nodes.label: Editable Name Pools (tools/name_pools.json)
nodes.rationale: Names stay editable but complexion eligibility must be preserved (e.g. Indian names for brown/dark complexions).

nodes.label: Foundation Asset Generation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: create_foundation_assets.py reads block geometry and profession IDs from Java and reproduces Phase 1 assets with Python + Pillow; players need neither Python nor an art service, and final Blockbench models can replace assets at the same IDs. It and create_village_marker.py merge shared language/axe-tag files to preserve each other's content.

nodes.label: Random-Spread Structure Placement
nodes.rationale: Plains/meadow biomes, spacing 40 chunks, separation 12, salt 18374629, with an exclusion zone around vanilla village candidates; joining the minecraft:village tag lets existing settlement discovery and naming recognize it.

nodes.label: Hometown Names and Settlements
nodes.rationale: Each resident keeps their first assigned hometown; renaming a village updates the suffix without changing identity.

nodes.label: Village Marker
nodes.rationale: Player-built settlements opt in via a placed marker (96-block radius); breaking it never deletes the settlement and no markers or terrain edits are placed automatically.

nodes.label: Combat Profession Lock
nodes.rationale: The first qualifying killing blow (including by its arrows) permanently locks the Knight or Archer role; assists do not lock.

nodes.label: Guard Level Progression (0-50)
nodes.rationale: Combat level independent of trading and friendship; each level adds 0.2 max HP and 0.5% damage while speed, cooldowns, draw time, accuracy and armor stay vanilla so equipment upgrades remain valuable. Advancing from L needs 20 + 3L XP; generated guards start at a UUID-seeded 15-30, newly trained guards at 0.

nodes.label: Pure Guard Policy vs Server Persistence Split
nodes.norm_label: pure guard policy vs server persistence split
nodes.rationale: GuardProgress and GuardDamageLedger hold pure balance/credit policy (unit-testable); GuardProgression owns server persistence and confirmed-death awards through the shared guard damage integration.

nodes.label: Village Life Animation Pack (99 clips)
nodes.rationale: Residents choose clips moment to moment (idles, trade work, hobbies, chats, greetings, reactions, weather); resource packs can add more packs.

nodes.label: Per-Player Co-op Relationship State
nodes.rationale: Affection, trust, visits, choices and memories belong to each player; physical requests belong to the resident and the first supplier keeps credit. The server validates choices, quests, recruitment and exchanges.

nodes.label: Resident-to-Resident Connections
nodes.rationale: Up to 16 persistent connections that grow with shared hobbies and values from spending days near each other.

nodes.label: Friendship Forgiveness for Player Hits
nodes.rationale: Unforgiven hits on any villager alert guards within 16 blocks; forgiveness requires the victim's effective Friend tier, and friendship with the responding guards does not excuse harming a different resident. Forgiven hits still cost trust.

nodes.label: Narrative Content Pack (content.json)
nodes.rationale: All personalities, story arcs, requests, gift preferences and dialogue live in data so authored text can expand without rewriting Java; /reload validates it and invalid packs keep the previous working definitions.

nodes.label: Gifts and Promises
nodes.rationale: Three gifts per player per day; rejected gifts consume neither item nor allowance. Withdrawing a promise costs five trust, harming a resident 15; apologies begin repair and story milestones stay recorded.

nodes.label: Four-Chapter Personal Stories
nodes.rationale: Stories progress through experiences and visits on different Minecraft days (confession after three visiting days; ending after five days and 60 trust); there are no request deadlines.

nodes.label: Relationship Tiers (New Neighbor to Best Friend)
nodes.norm_label: relationship tiers (new neighbor to best friend)
nodes.rationale: Points stop at 200 and gifts alone cannot unlock upper tiers; Friend and above also require shared history (shared experience, confession, completed story) so stories and activities drive progression rather than repeated gifting. No penalty for taking a break.

nodes.label: Milestone 7: Romance and Family (future)
nodes.rationale: Deferred until the friendship systems have been used in real worlds.

nodes.label: Shared Activities (Walk, Picnic, Exploration, Gathering)
nodes.rationale: Unlock at 15 points and 30 trust; occupy the single companion slot while active and award points/trust once per day.

nodes.label: Shared Gait Function (resident and armor models)
nodes.norm_label: shared gait function (resident and armor models)
nodes.rationale: Resident and armor models share one gait function so armor follows the stride; special vanilla poses and original face UV colors must stay intact.

nodes.label: Living Villagers (walking styles, breathing, articulated eyes)
nodes.norm_label: living villagers (walking styles, breathing, articulated eyes)
nodes.rationale: Six subtle walking styles, blinking/glancing eyes in each resident's original eye colors; clothing and armor follow the movement.

nodes.label: Ten Master Palettes
nodes.rationale: One palette colors the whole outfit (primary, secondary, accent, leather, metal, ink) with hand-shaded ramps.

nodes.label: Sims-style Men's and Women's Wardrobes
nodes.rationale: Palette-locked pixel art with 3D pieces; tops and bottoms mix freely except locked one-piece outfits; hair is chosen once per resident so a new job never changes it.

nodes.label: Focused Client GameTest Flags
nodes.rationale: runClientGameTest flags (-PfoundationOnly, -PstructuresOnly, -PguardsOnly, -PcompanionsOnly, -PoutfitsOnly, -PresidentSample, -PanimationPack, -PvillageGallery) run focused suites; test code lives in the gametest source set and is excluded from the release JAR.

nodes.label: Village Layout Simulation
nodes.rationale: simulate.py imitates jigsaw assembly on flat ground to balance pool weights and detect missing required buildings before testing in Minecraft; Minecraft remains the authority.

nodes.label: Replacement Pools and required_pools
nodes.rationale: Swap a building by changing its pool entry; the catalog derives required pools from required_pools so tests accept replacements without hard-coded names. Every blueprint must be referenced by a pool; stale NBT is deleted.

nodes.label: Structure Processors (worn roads, plank bridges, weathered stone)
nodes.norm_label: structure processors (worn roads, plank bridges, weathered stone)

nodes.label: In-Game Village Gallery (-PvillageGallery)
nodes.rationale: Places listed templates and whole villages on a superflat world and saves screenshots; a development aid outside the regression suite.

nodes.label: Village Layout Config (tools/village_layout.json, format 2)
nodes.rationale: Holds pools, weights, fallbacks, processors, depth (6), maximum distance (100), biomes, placement, slot_widths and required_pools.

nodes.label: Master Specification (Codex roadmap)
nodes.rationale: External specification supplying the Codex Phase 1 and Phase 2 roadmaps; where it gave no recipe the mod supplies initial ones.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Structures Verification
nodes.rationale: -PstructuresOnly exercises template loading, rotated bedrooms and door access, fixture block entities, twelve jigsaw assemblies, natural generation, professions/trades, hometown assignment and save/reload.

nodes.label: Codex Phase 2: Worldgen & Structures
nodes.rationale: Minecraft loads packaged JSON registries and compressed NBT templates directly from the mod.

nodes.label: Village Friends 2.12.0 Fabric Mod
nodes.rationale: Villagers get names, preferences, persistent memories, personal stories and player-shaped looks; conversations work offline with no AI account or service fees.

nodes.label: Independent Building Templates
nodes.rationale: Every building is one independent template with its own blueprint; improving or replacing one never touches the others and never requires Java edits.

nodes.label: Persistent Resident Identity (stable ID)
nodes.rationale: Stable ID independent of entity UUID and profession; zombie conversion/curing transfers identity, relationships, outcomes and names.

nodes.label: Civic Slots (priority 5)
nodes.rationale: Each plaza side has a large slot (<=17 wide), a street exit and a small slot (<=11 wide); priority 5 places the six civic buildings before any street can take their space.

nodes.label: Village Design Kit (kit.py, parts.py, roads.py)
nodes.rationale: Fills neighbour-derived states (fence/pane/wall connections, stair corners) because jigsaw pieces are placed with a known shape; checks every door has two clear blocks on both sides and measures bedrooms by flood fill.

nodes.label: Building Design Programs (DESIGNS = {name: function})
nodes.rationale: Each module in tools/village_design/buildings exposes DESIGNS; design_village.py runs them to write blueprints and --preview writes isometric previews.

nodes.label: Lot Contract (building_entrance jigsaw)
nodes.rationale: Exactly one north-edge villagefriends:building_entrance jigsaw at [x,1,0] (north_up, pool minecraft:empty, final state air, aligned joint); size 3-32; Y=0 is ground; doors need two clear blocks; homes need a recorded enclosed bedroom via b.room.

nodes.label: Lots (homes, workshops, decorations, empty gaps)
nodes.rationale: Streets at maximum depth only use plains/lots_outer so fields, paddocks and orchards gather on the outskirts; structure_void keeps natural ground in yards.

nodes.label: Village Jigsaw Graph
nodes.rationale: Town centre (random of 3) -> civic slots -> four exits -> avenues -> streets -> lot jigsaws (fallback street_ends and lots_outer), assembled by Minecraft's jigsaw system from ~60 templates.

nodes.label: Six Guaranteed Civic Buildings
nodes.rationale: Tavern, garrison with watchtower, carpenter-and-tailor workshop, chapel with graveyard, apothecary and library house eight of the ten new professions and their workstations.

nodes.label: Enclosed Bedrooms
nodes.rationale: Every home and most civic buildings have a solid enclosed bedroom with real two-part doors, a clear two-block route on each side and matched bed halves, so the future scanner can use layouts as fixtures.

nodes.label: Procedural Plains Village (villagefriends:village)
nodes.rationale: Typical village has 55-140 pieces, ~19 homes and 25-70 residents; all ten new professions appear in every village; new villages appear only in newly generated chunks.

nodes.label: Random Street Network
nodes.rationale: Four avenues grow into straights, S-bends, turns, tees, forks, crossroads and well squares; streets end in fading paths, lamp-and-bench ends or a timber gatehouse.

nodes.label: Town Centres (fountain square, village green, market square)
nodes.norm_label: town centres (fountain square, village green, market square)
nodes.rationale: 33x33 squares (central_plaza, plaza_green, plaza_market) started at random rotation; hold the notice board, benches, easel, music stand and bell. Plaza templates must keep villagefriends:town_start, painter and bard.

nodes.label: Vanilla Trade Workshops
nodes.rationale: Smithy, butcher, fletcher, shepherd, fisher, cartographer, mason and tannery give unemployed residents vanilla jobs.

nodes.label: Rigid Buildings with Terrain-Matching Streets
nodes.rationale: Buildings are rigid so doors and floors stay level; streets follow the ground column by column and become plank bridges over water; beard_thin blends foundations; depth six and 100-block distance bound the village.

nodes.label: Damage-Based Guard XP Credit
nodes.rationale: XP is awarded only on death, split by actual health damage dealt in the preceding 30 seconds; players and other damage take their share of the denominator, and contributions clear on unload/restart.

nodes.label: Patrols, Command Desk Controls and Shields (future)
nodes.norm_label: patrols, command desk controls and shields (future)

nodes.label: Empty Block Entity Integration Hooks
nodes.rationale: HousePlaque scanForBeds/scanForWorkstations, NoticeBoard refreshNotices, CommandDesk updatePatrolAssignments/refreshGuardRoster, ApothecaryCot updatePatient are intentionally empty with no tickers; housing, notice, patrol and patient state should get a versioned persistence schema when implemented.

nodes.label: Knight and Archer Spawn Eggs
nodes.rationale: Create ordinary equipped adult villagers at generated level 15-30; one point of trading XP keeps their jobs without workstations; no Survival recipe.

nodes.label: Child Villager Appearance
nodes.rationale: Children use a child model and play clothes; adult looks are revealed on growing up while identity and memories stay intact.

nodes.label: Locked One-Piece Outfits (locked_to)
nodes.rationale: Tops and bottoms mix freely within a set except where tags forbid it (armor, hose, kilt, sandals) or a top and bottom are locked_to each other, e.g. gowns, habits, jester's motley.

nodes.label: Supreme Casual Line (t101-t120, b101-b120)
nodes.rationale: New clothing stays casual medieval; the men's plain modern supreme casual line is the only exception.

nodes.label: Wardrobe Python Module Pipeline (tools/wardrobe)
nodes.rationale: Each piece is one Python module declaring its gender; shared shapes in kit.py (garments) and anime.py (hair) with per-set extras; every top must belong to an outfit template.

nodes.label: Grounded Anime-Inspired Hair Rule
nodes.rationale: Hair stays anime-inspired but grounded: pointed bangs, sidelocks, braids and buns, but no gravity-defying Goku/Vegeta spikes.
